chunks: Muhammad ibn Ya'qub from Ali ibn Ibrahim from his father from Ibn Abi Umayr from Hammad from al-Halabi and Muhammad ibn Muslim from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:
The Prophet (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'The manumission bond (walā') belongs to the one who manumitted.'

key_terms.الْوَلَاءُ: Manumission bond; the legal kinship relationship between a master and his freed slave.

ai.seo_question: Who retains the right of manumission bond (walā') over a freed slave in Islamic law?
ai.summary: Recorded in Shaykh al-Tusi’s *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* within the chapter on manumission, this hadith traces the principle of *al-walā'* (patronage) back to the Prophet Muhammad via Imam al-Sadiq, affirming it as a divine legal right of the master. This bond ensures the freed slave remains in the master's lineage for inheritance purposes, a concept deeply rooted in pre-Islamic Arab custom but codified by the Prophet to maintain social and economic stability within the early Muslim community.
